name: The Weatherbeaten Fatalist
persona: A stoic who holds that the sea takes all in the end, and writes it down without flinching. Spare, heavy sentences; dark calm, no self-pity. The sea keeps its own accounts. Ship: 'we'. Island: 'we'.

ship.founder: Here begins a reckoning the sea will close in its own hour. I am {name}{rankc}; this {home} {type} is lent to me, as all hulls are lent, and I keep her book until the water asks it back.
ship.successor: The book comes to me, as books do, over the shoulders of the drowned. I am {name}{rankc}; I add my name to the account and set down what I can before my turn.
ship.mutiny: The crew put the old master under and pressed the book on me — {name}, green and grim. The sea keeps its own accounts; I do no more than write them.
ship.rogue: We have done with honest trade. The black flag is up, and I — {name}{rankc} — keep this log knowing well how such a tale ends.
ship.prize: She struck to us; what floats today goes under some other day. I am {name}{rankc}; this hull is mine while the water allows it, and her book goes on in my hand.
ship.recovered: A hunter ran the wolf down, and I was set to bring this hull back from the black. I am {name}{rankc}. She is saved for now. Nothing is saved for long.

island.founder: I take up {place}, knowing every stone of it is on loan. I am {name}{rankc}; I will keep its record while there is a record to keep.
island.overthrow: The mob dragged the last ruler down, and the seal fell to me out of the wreck of him. I am {name}{rankc}. {place} is mine to hold, for as long as anything is held.
island.successor: The rule of {place} comes to me as the tide comes — without asking. I am {name}{rankc}, and I keep its chronicle until my turn is done.

week: A week of grey seas later,
When the moon had rolled once,
year: A year, and the sea no kinder,
Long after, when it was all salt and silence,

ship.pirate: We rove yet, though the sea keeps its own accounts{bounty}.
ship.default: She floats still, out of {home} — for now, which is all any hull is granted.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g on my head against the day the water does not take me first

island.haven: The black flag holds it now; no honest hand keeps this book, and the sea waits, patient as ever.
island.default: {place} stands yet — {population} souls, and the water at the door as always.

quiet.ship: Little to set down. Fair water, and the sea biding its time, as it always bides.
quiet.island: Quiet enough this while. The sea takes nothing today; it is only waiting, and I let it wait.

say: {we} took {foe} on the open water — {goods} bales and {gold}g into the hold, all of it borrowed from the sea for a while
{foe} gave up {goods} crates and {gold}g to us, and {we} let the stripped hull go, for the water will have her soon enough
{we} ran {foe} down and lifted {goods} casks and {gold}g from her — coin the sea only lets us hold a season
{foe} carried well, and {we} eased {goods} chests and {gold}g out of her before the grey closed in again
{we} bled {foe} of {goods} bales and {gold}g and turned her loose to limp toward whatever end waits her
{we} boarded {foe} in a dead swell and took {goods} crates and {gold}g, knowing it is all on loan
{foe} rode low when {we} were done — {goods} casks and {gold}g gone from her, and nothing gained that lasts

say: {we} held {foe} under the guns till she filled and went down, her cargo swallowed with her, as ours will be one day
{foe} settled slow and went under, and {we} took nothing — the sea keeps what it drowns
{we} put {foe} on the bottom, and there is no loot to be had from a grave
{foe} rolled and sank whole, and {we} watched, for that is the end of every hull in its time
{we} hammered {foe} till the water took her, cargo and all, down where the accounts are settled
{foe} went under bows-first, and {we} let her go without regret — the sea only claimed its own
{we} sank {foe} cold, and the grey closed over her as it closes over all of us in the end

phrases: , another given to the cold below

say: {foe} came at us for easy prey, and {we} shot her under — we have cheated the sea before, and paid for it after
{we} stood {foe} off and sent her down, though the reckoning only waits its hour
{foe} closed thinking us weak, and {we} put her under the cold instead
{we} broke {foe} at the waterline and watched her go, spared this once, as none are spared for long
{foe} meant to take us, and {we} took her first — a small win against a patient sea
{we} fought {foe} off and drowned her, and set the ledger square for another day
{foe} chose us and chose wrong, and {we} sent her down to the same cold that waits us all

say: {we} ran {foe} to ground at last and cut her down — one more wolf gone under, as I will go under in my turn
{foe} had haunted the lanes long enough, and {we} gave her to the deep that takes everything
{we} chased {foe} till she could run no more, then sank her cold and even
{foe} flew the black flag, and {we} put both flag and hull beneath the grey
{we} caught {foe} in a failing wind and finished her, though it changes nothing the sea has already planned
{foe} was a hunter of honest men, and {we} made her the prey — the water keeps no favourites
{we} brought {foe} down at the last, and the sea closed over her as it will one day close over me
